THE HOLDING MUSEUM'S METADATA
  title:            歷史文化園區-107-com-pa-91-re-202006272036525ef724c04bc9c0.jpg
  description:      ​金岳的歷史文化園區顧名思義即為我們歷史及文化的重要場域，亦是隨著金岳社區發展協會推動社區營造過程中所建立的文化傳承里程碑。本協會自2005年正式運作後，首先建立眺望台及穀倉，從兩棟傳統建築開始推動社區營造；2006年建立部落涼亭，期望將部落市集與族人休憩空間結合起來；2009年建立傳統屋及莎韻之鐘，重新讓我們能以自己的聲音訴說莎韻之鐘的故事，並透過傳統屋讓大家認識南澳群的半穴室，且有石板屋頂的家屋形式，逐年形成了歷史文化園區。此空間為部落重要的入口位置，為一群傳統建物圍繞的停車場，腹地廣大，具備歷史、文化、生活、教育、交通節點與旅遊服務等功能。本協會於2012年為改善水泥停車場空間過大，以大區塊的文化地景規劃，建立具有特色的入口意象，展現獨具特色的金岳泰雅文化，並結合休憩、休閒、生活、故事與綠美化之景觀營造，打造一個多功能的入口文化導覽資訊站，成為遊客認識部落的第一站。另外，此空間亦為本部落每年舉辦傳統祭儀主要空間，反映與舊部落連結的精神象徵與意涵，透過每年的活動凝聚部落共識，更成為本部落重要文化活動。

Een huipil wordt uitsluitend door vrouwen gebruikt om de bovenkant van het lichaam (romp, schouders) te bedekken.

  title:            One of Myanmar’s ethic, Karen lady showing off her dress while smiling and gazing at the sky with a pensive thought in the bamboo forest.jpg
  description:      This photo was taken in Pyin Oo Lwin (May Myo), Mandalay Division, Myanmar, and captures the powerful presence of a young Karen woman standing proudly in her traditional dress. She wears a long white cheh gua — a garment worn by unmarried Karen women to symbolize purity — while gazing upward beneath the bamboo canopy, embodying pride, freedom, and cultural identity. In Karen tradition, clothing is more than just fabric; it is a statement of who you are — your age, marital status, and place within the community. Every garment is handwoven on a backstrap loom, with patterns that carry generation

in June 1855. This conflict between the Modoc In-

troying the Native fishing waters in the Lower Soda
Springs area. Settlers led by Squire Reuben Gibson
and Mountain Joe Doblondy, with local Indians led
by their chief Weilputus, engaged Modocs, killed
their chief Dorcas Dalla, and dispersed them. Poet

  title:            Carving instrument used to make ivory dentures, Europe, 1701 Wellcome L0057114.jpg
  description:      Different tools were used to make dentures, including saws and polishers. This tool would have been used to carve marks in the dentures to create the appearance of individual teeth. Dentures of this period were made from a small range of materials, including ivory. This example was carved from hippopotamus ivory and would have been expensive. Ivory was difficult to clean and over time began deteriorate and smell quite unpleasant. The tool is shown here with a denture made from hippopotamus ivory (A600140).

  title:            Carving instrument used to make ivory dentures, Europe, 1701 Wellcome L0057114.jpg
  description:      Different tools were used to make dentures, including saws and polishers. This tool would have been used to carve marks in the dentures to create the appearance of individual teeth. Dentures of this period were made from a small range of materials, including ivory. This example was carved from hippopotamus ivory and would have been expensive. Ivory was difficult to clean and over time began deteriorate and smell quite unpleasant. The tool is shown here with a denture made from hippopotamus ivory (A600140).

  title:            Brooklyn Museum 85.143 Hemba Mask.jpg
  description:      Among the Suku of the southwestern part of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, masks plays crucial role in protecting boys during initiation, the vulnerable period between boyhood and manhood. The power contained in Hemba masks may be directed against those who disrespect or attempt to harm the initiates, or it may be used to cure illness and promote prosperity. Often brightly colored and surmounted by animal figures, these masks depict past elders and lineage heads—people who command a great deal of respect and who make important decisions affecting the community.

  description:      Adinkra Alphabet is a phonetic writing system based on Adinkra symbols, used for writing Akan, Ewe, Ga and Dagbani languages. It consists of 10 vowels and 32 consonants, with no distinction between upper and lowercase characters. Each character has a unique numerical value. The character "⊃" serves as a vowel marker, while "✕" marks mathematical arrays. The Nyame Dua character, which appears last in the alphabet, marks numbers. Any character placed between two Nyame Dua characters is interpreted as a number.

  title:            Famadihana MPMF24.jpg
  description:      This photo shows Famadihana, a Malagasy tradition also known as the "turning of the dead." It's a ceremony where the remains of ancestors are exhumed, wrapped in new shrouds, and often danced with before being reburied in new tombs. It's a way for the Malagasy people to show respect for their ancestors and to renew family ties. This is a culture that only the Malagasy people practice.

THE HOLDING MUSEUM'S METADATA
  title:            FAMADIHANA MPMF24.jpg
  description:      Famadihana is a deeply rooted cultural practice in Malagasy society, where it's believed that the dead continue to influence the lives of the living. The ceremony is often accompanied by songs, dances, and festivities, and it's generally organized every 5 to 7 years, though this can vary by region and family. Some view Famadihana as a way to celebrate life and the continuity of generations, while others consider it a religious or spiritual practice.

  title:            Itsekri Flag RMG RP33-001.jpg
  description:      Itsekri Flag
The personal flag of Itsekiri chief Nana Olomu (1852-1916). The background of the design is yellow, with a printed Union Flag inserted (upside down) in the canton. Near the top edge is the name 'NANNA' in dark blue letters, below, the flag is painted with a naked man shooting a leopard. The flag is made of wool bunting, the applied lettering is hand sewn while the seams of the flag are machine sewn. It has a linen hoist containing a rope. The flag was captured during the expedition of 1894.

  title:            Carving instrument used to make ivory dentures, Europe, 1701 Wellcome L0057114.jpg
  description:      Different tools were used to make dentures, including saws and polishers. This tool would have been used to carve marks in the dentures to create the appearance of individual teeth. Dentures of this period were made from a small range of materials, including ivory. This example was carved from hippopotamus ivory and would have been expensive. Ivory was difficult to clean and over time began deteriorate and smell quite unpleasant. The tool is shown here with a denture made from hippopotamus ivory (A600140).
